baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the deck assembly fasteners, panel, plywood, decking and plate dimensions faithfully. Set B correctly separates the 3/8" x 4" HEX THROUGH BOLT from the 3/8" X 4" HEX BOLT as two distinct fasteners, each supported by its own quote. Set A collapses these into a single 'hex bolt' claim whose quote is actually the through bolt, misbinding the label and dropping the separate hex bolt used at the railing post bracket.
baseline-first.remarks: The text layer lists both '3/8" x 4" HEX THROUGH BOLT' and '3/8" X 4" HEX BOLT' (the latter at the railing post bracket and in the A5 deck-to-house detail), so treating them as one component loses a real distinction. Both sets leave out the Clearvue cable railing, railing post bracket and adjustable scaffold footing, but those are largely labels rather than dimensional claims.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the material and fastener specs accurately, but A distinguishes the two distinct bolt callouts on the page: '3/8" x 4" HEX THROUGH BOLT' (deck module detail) and '3/8" X 4" HEX BOLT' (railing attachment). B collapses these into a single 'hex bolt' claim whose quote actually reads 'HEX THROUGH BOLT', so the quote does not support the stated entity and the separate hex bolt item is lost. Otherwise the shared claims are faithful, with correct values, units and conditions.
variant-first.remarks: The page lists two visually similar but separately labeled bolts ('HEX THROUGH BOLT' in the deck module detail and 'HEX BOLT' in the railing attachment); extractions should keep them as distinct items rather than merging on the generic term 'hex bolt'.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are effectively identical: same 19 claims, same values and quotes, differing only in that A labels the HSS4X4X1/4 claim 'member' and B labels it 'structural member'. Both bind values loosely (generic 'dimension'/'component' entities, no section or grid context), and both repeat W10X15 under two names. Neither set misreads a value or invents a figure, so neither is preferable.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions treat every dimension as 'dimension | length' with no reference to which member, span or detail it belongs to (e.g. 3'-7", 5'-3", 8" are the small dimensions near C5/S-511 in Section 1), which loses most of the engineering meaning. W10X15 is stated twice (once as 'component | specification', once as 'First Floor Framing | member section'). Section labels (STRUCTURAL SECTION 1 / 4) and grid lines present on the page would be useful binding context and are absent from both sets.

variant-first.note: The two sets are effectively identical in content: the same 19 claims, same values, same quotes, with only trivial wording differences ("structural member" vs "member" for HSS4X4X1/4) and ordering. Both bind W10X15 to "First Floor Framing" although it appears in Structural Section 1, both duplicate the PL3"X1/4" and W10X15 facts under two names, and both use vague entities such as "dimension | length" and "component | specification". variant-first.remarks: Both extractions treat every dimension string as "dimension | length", losing which member, spacing or offset each dimension belongs to (e.g. 6'-0" and 5'-0" are horizontal grid spacings, 8"/6"/10" are small offsets). The claim "First Floor Framing | member section | W10X15" is unsupported: W10X15 is labeled in STRUCTURAL SECTION 1, and the page part shows sections, not a first-floor framing plan. W8X13, HSS4X6X1/4 and L3x3x1/4" are clearly labeled on the page but captured by neither set.

Both also repeat several facts under two names (e.g. NFDS rating, main-breaker rating, panel phase, #4G and #10G ground sizes) and both omit schedule rows 50, 33 and 10 plus the main bonding jumper and sensor circuits.

Shared gaps: wiring schedule rows 50 (AL: 3#6, #8G., 1"C.), 33 (CU: 6#10, 3#10G., 1"C.) and 10 (CU: #12/2WG.), the MAIN BONDING JUMPER note, and the voltage/current sensor circuits to the organizer instrumentation panel. Text layer scrambles schedule row numbers (e.g. "31"/"32" trailing the description lines), but the image confirms the row-to-description pairing used by both sets.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts from the notes and wiring schedule, with identical quotes and largely identical claims. The only substantive difference is the NFDS enclosure claim: Set A correctly names the device simply "NFDS" as the page does, while Set B invents the qualifier "DC NFDS" for a device the page never describes as DC. baseline-first.remarks: Both sets repeat several facts under two names (MAIN BREAKER rating 150 A vs 150A/2P; NFDS rating 200A/2P vs 200 A; MAIN PANEL phase '1 phase' vs '1'; GND connection conductor vs wire size; Wiring 150 #4G ground wire vs ground conductor size; Wiring 34 #10G ground conductor vs ground wire). variant-first.note: Both sets are essentially identical in content and quotes, drawing on the same page-context callouts (rod, stiffener plate, angle, threaded rod, elevations, W8X10, neoprene pad, hex nut, base plate, channel, A325 bolts). Set B adds one extra claim that merely repeats the '3 1/2" STEEL ROD' diameter already claimed, so it is a pure duplicate. variant-first.remarks: The visible page image shows only empty GENERAL SHEET NOTES / REFERENCE KEYNOTES / SHEET KEYNOTES tables; all quoted callouts come from the surrounding page text, so quote fidelity could only be checked against that text layer. 'Grade Level | elevation | 0"' is a near-trivial datum claim, and 'Channel | section | C3X6 1/4"' looks like a merged/garbled callout (section plus a separate 1/4" dimension) in both sets.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (solar altitude 50°, window azimuth 0, the louver spacing algorithm and its D*1.2 simplification, 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, truncated isosceles triangle profile, powder-coated finish, 25° structural bend) and both are heavily padded with duplicate restatements of the same facts under slightly different entity/attribute names. Set A repeats three facts twice each (spacing formula, louver shape, bend angle), while Set B repeats four (bend angle, finish, spacing algorithm, shape) and additionally misattributes the 'optimal solar illumination' outcome to the powder-coated finish alone, whereas the page credits the screen's transparency and finish together. Set A is therefore marginally cleaner, with one fewer duplicate pair and no misbound quote, though neither set captures the proportional reduction of louver spacing based on average profile widths.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets are dominated by near-duplicate claims (same value/quote restated under 'louver' vs 'Harvest Shade Screen louver', and 'shape' vs 'tapered into...', and 'spacing formula' vs 'spacing simplified formula'), which inflates apparent coverage without adding facts. Both also omit the stated design adjustment that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths, and neither notes that the 1:1 ratio provided optimal insulation from direct radiant heat gain. Set A's condition string 'along the louver longit' is a truncated quote fragment.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same eight facts — window azimuth 0, 50° solar altitude at fall equinox noon, the louver spacing algorithm and its simplified Height = D*1.2, the 1:1 depth-to-height ratio, the tapered truncated isosceles triangle louver profile, the 25° longitudinal structural bend, and the powder-coated finish. A states every value in full and correctly bound, whereas B truncates the bend condition ('along the louver longit') and records the simplified formula as the bare fragment 'D*1.2' while pushing the general formula into its conditions field. Both repeat facts under two names (four pairs in A, three in B), so A's only real drawback is slightly greater redundancy.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets miss the stated design fact that louver spacing was proportionally reduced based on the average of the profile widths (after the taper), and neither captures the 25° bend's function of directing reflected light onto the ceiling/adjacent louvers and reducing direct glare, nor the screen transparency noted alongside the powder-coated finish. A states the powder-coated finish twice under two names ('louver' and 'Harvest Shade Screen'); the text attributes it to the screen, so the louver binding is a mild relabeling rather than a separate fact. B's claim 1 is a near-duplicate of its claim 9 with the formula split awkwardly between value and conditions.

variant-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical: 14 of 15 claims match exactly and all are correctly bound to their Wiring Schedule rows (150/151 and circuits 20, 31, 32, 33, 50), with quotes that support them. The only difference is the row-151 conductor claim: Set A states 'conductor quantity and size = 3#4/0', while Set B states a vaguer 'conductor = 3#4/0' with conditions AL and ARMORED CABLE that are already covered by its separate material and cable-type claims. Both sets omit the main-panel note facts (120/240V 1Ø 3W, 50A/2P main breaker, 200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R enclosure) and several row details (e.g., 150's 2-1/2"C., 31's 3/4"C., 50's #8G., rows 10 and 34).
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions ignore the NOTES block above the schedule (main panel voltage/configuration, main breaker and NFDS ratings, NEMA 3R enclosure) — an important engineering fact both sets miss. Set B's row-151 'conductor' attribute is generic and its AL / ARMORED CABLE conditions duplicate its own separate claims for that row. Both add the unit 'AWG' to '#12G' for circuit 20, which is not written on the page (minor). The text layer garbles the panel note lines (e.g. 'MAIN BONDI', '00A/2P NFDS') and shows '3#10G.' for row 33 where the image reads '10G.'; the image is the clearer source for those items.

baseline-first.note: Both sets are drawn from the same wiring schedule rows and are essentially identical: 14 of the 15 claims match exactly, and the only difference (Set A's 151 conductor claim with AL/ARMORED CABLE conditions vs Set B's 151 'conductor quantity and size' claim) is correct in both forms. All values are bound to the right symbol rows per the image (e.g., 150 = AL: 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.; 33 = CU: 6#10, #10G., 1"C.; 32 = CU: 2#10USE-2), and quotes support the claims. baseline-first.remarks: Text layer is garbled and out of order (symbol numbers detached from their description strings, 'MAIN BONDI' truncated, '00A/2P NFDS' cut off at the left margin), so the image table was used as the authority. Both sets name the same kind of entity inconsistently ('Circuit 33' vs 'Wiring Schedule 150' for symbol numbers in the SYMBOL column); normalizing this would help. Both sets also omit the NOTES block (main panel MP, 120/240V, 1-phase 3W, 50A/2P main breaker, 200A/2P NFDS, NEMA 3R enclosure), which contains real engineering facts.

The MWB02 quote in Set A ('MWB02 CTION CENTER MODU') is a text-layer/OCR merge of the A1/A3 'CENTER MODULE MILLWORK SECTION' title with the MWB02 mark, so that claim cannot be verified from the quote. Several 3' - 0" and 5" values appear multiple times on the sheet with no unambiguous component binding in the text layer, so both sets' assignments of those values are partly guesswork.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds the laundry-section dimensions (2' - 5 1/16" width, 7' - 0 1/8" height) and the bulkhead, platform and clearances correctly, while Set B omits both laundry dimensions and adds a misbound East Island "component width" of 3' - 0" (that value is a counter/height dimension) plus a trivial, garbled MWB02 "component type" claim. Set B also repeats the same facts more often (platform height 6" twice, the 3' - 0" height restated three times as Island, East Island and "millwork unit"), and its quote for the MWB02 claim is a text-layer fragment. Set A's weaknesses are vaguer entities ("millwork", "millwork section") and a spurious "inches" unit on two material values, and it misses the 3' - 3 3/4" North Island dimensions that B captures. baseline-first.remarks: Both sets treat the 5" value twice, once as backsplash height and once as East Island countertop thickness; the page shows two 5" callouts but a 5" countertop thickness is questionable and one of these bindings may be wrong in both sets. Both sets also omit the 2' - 0" and 6 1/2" dimensions present in the text layer. Set A appends the unit 'inches' to material specifications (1/2" MDF FIN. W/ P3, 3/4" MDF GABLE FIN. W/ P3), which is a unit/formatting error rather than a content error. Set B's quote 'MWB02 CTION CENTER MODU' is a text-layer overlap artifact and should not be used as evidentiary text.

Shared issues: dimension claims such as 'dimension | value | 8"' or 'dimension | length | 9'-0"' carry no component or what-is-measured binding, so they are vague and not verifiable against a specific detail; 'plate | size | 3"X1/4"' duplicates the PL3"X1/4" section claim; 9'-0" and 2'-4" are each claimed twice. variant-first.note: Both sets capture the main equipment ratings (2.8 kW inverter, 50 A/2P main breaker, 60 A DC NFDS, 200 A/2P NFDS, junction box) with supporting quotes. Set B correctly quotes the 60A DC NFDS note for the DC NFDS enclosure claim and additionally extracts the 200A/2P NFDS enclosure type with its own quote. Wiring schedule entries (e.g. 150 AL: 3#4/0, #4G., 2-1/2"C.) are only partially extracted (ground conductor and conduit omitted), and the NEC 690.42 exception / ground-fault bonding note is not claimed by either set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the main equipment ratings (2.8 kW inverter, 50A/2P main breaker, 60A and 200A NFDS, 120/240V sub-panel) with supporting quotes, and both make the same error of binding '3W' to 'phase' when the note reads 1-phase, 3-wire. baseline-first.remarks: Both sets misread '1, 3W' on the SUB-PANEL PV note: 1 is the phase count and 3W the wire count, so the 'phase = 3 W' claim in both is misbound. The wiring schedule quotes are truncated (e.g. '150 AL: 3#4/0' drops the ground/conduit details), and the NEC 690.42 exception note (conductor-to-ground bond by the GFCI device) is not extracted by either set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets extract the same core Table 6-1 values correctly (TwFAStif, TwSSStif, TwGJStif, TwEAStif, TwFAIner, TwSSIner at the base and top rows, plus the 347,460 kg integrated tower mass), with no misread or misbound values in either. Set B adds two extra correct claims (TwFAcgOf and TwSScgOf = 0.0 m at Elevation 87.60 m), but these are trivial zero-value entries of little engineering use. Both sets repeat nearly every fact two or three times (under unit variants like kg•m vs kg*m and with/without HtFract), and both omit the TMassDen column entirely and the tower mass center at 38.234 m. Given equal correctness and equal duplication, the two extra trivial claims in B do not make it meaningfully better.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets omit the entire TMassDen (kg/m) column of Table 6-1 and the statement that the integrated tower mass is centered at 38.234 m (sentence is cut off in the text layer but the value is legible). Each set states most facts 2-3 times, differing only in unit notation (kg•m vs kg*m, N•m2 vs N*m^2) or in whether HtFract is included in conditions — effectively the same claim under two names. Many quotes are reconstructed with '...' rather than literal contiguous text, though the values they point to are correct.

variant-first.note: Both sets transcribe Table 6-1 correctly: every stiffness, inertia and cg-offset value is bound to the right property and the right Elevation/HtFract row, and the overall tower mass (347,460 kg) is quoted accurately. The sets are identical except that A adds two more zero cg-offset entries (TwFAcgOf and TwSScgOf = 0.0 m at Elevation 87.60 m), which are correct but of negligible engineering content since both offsets are zero at every station. Both sets repeat the same facts two or three times (e.g. TwFAStif 115.82E+9 at 87.60 m, TwSSStif 614.34E+9 at 0.00 m) and both omit the TMassDen column and the 38.234 m mass-center location. Each set states 8 of its claims twice (unit notation varies between N•m2 and N*m^2 for the same fact). Several quotes use '...' reconstructions rather than literal page text; values are still correct. Coverage is limited to the 0.00 m and 87.60 m rows; the intermediate nine rows are unclaimed in both.

variant-first.note: B correctly records the datum elevations and level distances (T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", Grade Level to First Floor 2'-4", First Floor to T.O. Steel 9'-0") and the grid spans, whereas A misbinds the 9'-0" and 2'-4" level dimensions to "Column C1" and treats the section/detail callouts C1, C3, C5 and A3 as columns. variant-first.remarks: Both extractions bind most raw dimensions to placeholder entities ("Structural Member", "Section 1", "vertical dimension") instead of the beams/columns they dimension; the callout bubbles (C1/C3/C5/A3 with sheet refs) are section/detail marks, not columns, and A repeatedly treats them as columns. A's two W10X12 claims ("left side" and "bottommost visible beam") may be the same fact stated twice. B repeats the 2'-4" and 9'-0" level distances under both a named and a generic entity. Neither shown sample captures the W8X13/W8X10/W10X12/L3x3x1/4 member labels of Section 1 or the HSS4X6X1/4 and W6X20/L3X3X1/4 labels of Section 4, though these may sit in the unshown shared claims.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims about the sub-panel, inverters, NFDS units and junction box, and both repeat the 3-wire and NEMA 3R facts under two names and both misbind 'ground fault' to the Main Breaker when the note attributes it to the inverter's ground fault protection device. Set A additionally captures the substantive note-4 content (ground fault protection required per the NEC 690.42 exception), which Set B only reduces to a vague 'compliance' claim, but A also misreads the label 20 as a wire size and invents a 20→34 connection. Set B's extras are almost entirely trivia (labels 20 and 34, 'terminal value' claims), one of which misplaces the value 4 at the lower terminal when 31 is the lower label. On balance A carries the more important engineering fact despite its two bad claims.
variant-first.remarks: The circled numbers 20/31/4/34/5 are diagram reference or terminal labels, not wire sizes or ratings; both extractions try to turn them into engineering values. Both sets also state the 3-wire configuration three times (PV Equipment wire configuration, PV Equipment wire count, SUB-PANEL PV wire count) and the NEMA 3R sub-panel enclosure twice. The note-4 fact that the required conductor-to-ground bond is made by the ground fault protection device is only weakly represented in either set.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the notes correctly for the sub-panel, inverters, the two NFDS and the junction box, and both share the same errors: ground fault protection misbound to the Main Breaker with a fabricated quote, an invented 4→31 connection between callout numbers, and 3W/phase attributed to a generic "PV Equipment" instead of the SUB-PANEL PV. Set A adds two clearly misread claims treating the diagram callouts 20 and 4 as terminal values of a "PV Equipment Circuit 1", plus two trivial label claims and a loose "compliance: NEC 690.42 EXCEPTION" claim that drops the conductor-to-ground bond condition. Set B keeps that NEC 690.42 EXCEPTION as a condition on the inverter ground-fault claim with a supporting quote, and its only extra errors are one callout read as a wire size and one invented 20→34 connection. On balance B has fewer wrong claims and the better-grounded inverter/NEC claim.
baseline-first.remarks: The numbers 20, 31, 34, 4, 5 in the diagram are note/detail callouts on symbols, not wire sizes, terminal values or component identifiers; both extractors misread them. Both sets also lose the distinct fact of note 4 that the required conductor-to-ground bond is made by the ground fault protection device under the NEC 690.42 exception. The text layer garbles the phase symbol (1□) and truncates quotes; the quote 'MAIN BREAKER TER WITH GROUND FAULT' in both sets appears to be a splice of 'MAIN BREAKER' and 'INVERTER WITH GROUND FAULT' and is not on the page.

baseline-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (dishwasher temperatures, sensor count, capacity, heated-drying disablement, and the clothes-drying scoring thresholds) and both repeat several facts under two names. Set A states the 115°F half-points condition correctly, including that the sensor must not reach 120°F, and its quotes match the page. Set B misquotes the wash/rinse requirement ('at least one wash and rinse and cycle') and drops the 'does not reach 120°F' condition from one of its 115°F claims, while adding an extra duplicate of the heated-drying claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets heavily duplicate facts (sensor count, 120°F, 115°F, and each scoring threshold appear twice under different entity/attribute names), inflating claim counts without adding information. Both also omit notable page facts: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of two sensor readings, or lower if the higher sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption', cycle-completion confirmation by audible/visible signal, permitted load states (empty/partial/fully loaded, soiled or clean), the two-loads-per-day requirement with separate scoring, and the demonstration requirement for visible drying methods.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts (dishwasher capacity, 120°F/115°F thresholds, two sensors, heated-drying disablement, clothes-drying eligibility and the Figure 8 scoring bands) and both are heavily padded with duplicate restatements of the same facts under different entity/attribute names. Set A additionally garbles one quote ('at least one wash and rinse and cycle' instead of 'wash and rinse cycle'), while Set B's quotes are all faithful. Set B also has slightly fewer duplicate pairs (7 vs 8), making it marginally cleaner and more accurate overall.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets miss several substantive facts on the page: the temperature-of-record rule (higher of the two sensor readings, or the lower if the higher sensor is defective), the definition of cycle 'interruption' (8-5e), cycle completion confirmed by audible/visible signal (8-5f), the allowed load states (empty/partial/full, soiled or clean, 8-5h), the two-loads-per-day requirement and separate scoring of each load (item d), and the requirement that towel-visible drying methods be demonstrated to the architecture and market appeal juries (item c). Both sets also duplicate the same facts under two entity names (e.g., 'Clothes Dryer Subcontest' vs 'clothes-drying task'; 'dishwasher' vs 'Dishwasher'), inflating claim counts without adding information.

baseline-first.note: Set A covers the wiring schedule rows more completely, including symbol 31 (material, conductor configuration, conduit size) and the conductor-configuration details for symbols 32, 33, 34, 50, 150 and 151, all read correctly against the table. Set B's 14 claims are all accurate and cleanly bound, but it omits the entire symbol 31 row and most conductor-configuration facts, so it drops real engineering content. A's only real flaw is redundancy: symbol 33 and symbol 34 conductor configurations are each stated twice (once with and once without the ground conductors), and the ground conductors are also captured under a separate attribute. Otherwise both sets bind values to the right rows and their quotes support the claims.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets omit wiring schedule rows 20 (CU: 3#12, #12G., 3/4"C.) and 10 (CU: #12/2WG.); Set B additionally omits row 31 entirely. In Set A the 'conductor configuration' claims that include the ground conductors (e.g. '6#10, 3#10G.', '2#10, #10G.', '3#4/0, #4G.') overlap the separate ground-conductor claims and each other, which is a splitting/deduplication pattern worth normalizing (keep ungrounded conductors in 'conductor configuration' and grounds only in 'ground conductor').

variant-first.note: Set B covers the wiring schedule more completely: it captures the main conductor configurations for the rows (3#6 for 50, 6#10 for 33/34, 2#10 for 31, 3#4/0 for 150/151) and includes symbol 31, all of which Set A omits. Set A is clean and every claim is correctly bound, but it never states the phase conductor size/count for any row and skips rows 31, 20 and 10 entirely. B's weaknesses are redundancy (the same conductor facts repeated under 'conductor' and 'conductor configuration' for 151, 33, 34) and one imprecise binding, calling 32's '2#10USE-2' a conductor configuration when USE-2 is the cable type. Both sets read the values, units and the AL/ARMORED CABLE conditions on 151 correctly.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets omit schedule rows 20 (CU: 3#12, #12G., 3/4"C.) and 10 (CU: #12/2WG.). B's 'conductor configuration' attribute is inconsistently scoped (sometimes includes the ground conductor, e.g. '6#10, 3#10G.', sometimes only the phase conductors, e.g. '6#10'), producing near-duplicate claims; entity naming also alternates between 'Wiring Symbol n' and 'Symbol n' for the same row.

variant-first.note: B captures the 2" x 8" deck frame and states the A6 'LANDSCAPE FOOTING 18"' size as a plain dimension, whereas A omits the frame and turns the 18" callout into an unsupported 'depth'. Both bind the 1" to 'nut sleeve' even though the text layer separates '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE', and both repeat the joist and reclaimed-wood facts. B's extra coverage is partly offset by two misbound claims (4 1/4" as a 'component width' and 1'-0" as the C1 plan's 'overall depth'), so the margin is small.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets bind '1"' to 'nut sleeve' although the text layer lists '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' as separate items; the 1" belongs to the nut. Both omit the A6 hardware/post facts (3/4" THREADED ROD, 1" NUT, SLEVE, 4X4 TO BE CUT AS NEEDED, 8'-0") and the 3 3/4"/1 1/4" footing dimensions. The 4 1/4" values in A6 appear twice and their target component is ambiguous in the text layer, so any claim binding them needs an explicit component. Generic quotes such as '1'-0"' occur in several details (C1 and A6) and do not by themselves identify which dimension is meant.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims and the same defects: each duplicates the joist and reclaimed-surface facts, and each merges the separate labels '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' into a single 'nut sleeve' of 1". A adds genuinely supported facts B lacks — the 2" X 8" FRAME member, the 18" landscape footing size stated without inventing an attribute, and the 3" = 1'-0" A6 scale. B's only unique claims are weaker: 'deck surface width 5 1/2"' re-binds the plywood deck's width to a vague entity, and 'landscape footing depth 18"' asserts a depth the sheet never states. A's own extras are not clean ('component width 4 1/4"' and 'decking footing plan overall depth 1'-0"' misbind detail/plan dimensions), but it still nets more correct content.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets miss several real facts on the sheet: 3/4" THREADED ROD, 1" NUT (as its own item), SLEVE, 4X4 TO BE CUT AS NEEDED, the 8'-0" dimension in A6, the 3 3/4"/1 1/4" connection dims, the 7 1/2"/1 1/2"/3 1/2" plan dims, and the C1/B1/C3 scales (6"=1'-0", 1 1/2"=1'-0", 1"=1'-0"). The text layer garbles 'SLEEVE' as 'SLEVE' and runs '1" NUT' and 'SLEVE' together, which likely caused both extractors to invent a 'nut sleeve' of 1". 'LANDSCAPE FOOTING 18"' is a detail title whose 18" is ambiguous (footing size vs depth), so neither set can bind it confidently; likewise the 4 1/4" (x2) and 1'-0" dims in A6 are hard to attribute to width/thickness from the raster alone.

baseline-first.note: Set A covers the Module B (C1) member systematically — total length 10'-3 3/4", the three horizontal segments (3'-8 3/8", 3'-6", 3'-1 5/16", which sum to the total) and the 3/8" THROUGH BOLT — plus the Module A right segment, all supported by the text layer. Set B instead adds the Module A total length 12'-3 3/4", the L3X3X1/4 angle profile and the Module A left segment (2'-3 7/8" + 7'-0" + 2'-11 7/8" = 12'-3 3/4"), but drops the entire Module B dimension set and the fastener, so it omits more important facts. Both sets repeat facts under two names (A: 2'-5 5/16" and 3"; B: 4" and 1'-11 1/8") and both attach unverifiable witness-line conditions to the base-plate dimensions, where A's "hole center height 2\" from bottom" and B's "width 4 3/4\" from edge of post to edge of plate" (self-contradictory) are the weakest readings. On balance A is the more complete and more faithful set.
baseline-first.remarks: The base-plate/base-block dimension strings (3", 4 3/4" / 4 13/16", 2", 4") are too small in the image to confirm which witness lines they span, so both sets' conditions on these values are guesses; A calls the same object 'base block' and B 'base plate'/'base block' inconsistently. Both sets also carry 'component B | width | 6 3/16"' although 6 3/16" is one of the vertical segment dimensions (1'-11 1/8" + 6 3/16" = 2'-5 5/16"), i.e. likely misbound in both. Set B's support-post claim has a malformed value string (stray trailing quote). Shared vague entities ('component', 'PV detail', 'beam') appear in both and were not penalized asymmetrically.

variant-first.note: Set B correctly binds the Module B (detail C1) segment lengths 3'-8 3/8", 3'-6" and 3'-1 5/16", its total length 10'-3 3/4", and the 3/8" THROUGH BOLT fastener, all of which Set A omits; Set A also invents detailed base-plate conditions and misbinds 1'-11 1/8" as a support post height on top of already stating it as a detail segment. Set A does capture facts B misses: Module A total length 12'-3 3/4", its left segment 2'-3 7/8", and the L3X3X1/4 member profile. Both sets repeat the same values under two or three names and use vague entities (component, beam, PV detail, base block), but B's bindings to the named modules are more faithful overall.
variant-first.remarks: Base-plate/base-block dimensions (3", 4 3/4" vs 4 13/16", 2", 4") are hard to resolve at this image scale; the two sets bind them to different properties (plate width vs. block spacing; horizontal hole offset vs. hole center height) and at least one binding in each set is probably wrong, so those were only lightly weighted. Note 4 3/4" (A1) and 4 13/16" (C1) differ between details while the other base dims repeat, which suggests that dimension is a varying spacing/offset rather than a fixed plate size. Both sets also leave out other page values (1 1/2", 5/8", 7 1/16", 2'-2 7/8", 6 13/16", 1'-8 11/16", 4 13/16"), though as samples that is not penalized.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core readings of Figures 2-10, including several conflicting near-duplicate values (mass density 3,100 vs 3,000 kg/m at r/R=0, axial 4.5e10 vs 4.7e10 N at r/R=0, torsional 0.9e11 vs 1.0e11 N·m^2 at r/R=0, and 0 vs 100 kg/m at the tip). Set A's two extra claims on Figure 2-11 are both wrong: 2 m at the root is the blade planform edge, not the geometric center (near 0.3 m), and −4 m is the axis minimum, not the shear center at r/R=0.2 (near 0.1 m). Set B's extras are better — torsional ≈0.8e11 N·m^2 at the root matches the curve — though its flap 1.2e11 N·m^2 at the root misreads a y-axis tick (the curve starts near 1.5e11) and it repeats the axial tip claim. On balance B makes fewer wrong claims, so it is the better set.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets quote only concatenated axis labels, legend entries and tick numbers, so no quote actually supports the numeric value claimed (e.g. 'Mass density [kg/m] ... Nondimensional Blade Span (r/R)' cannot support 3100 kg/m). Both sets also emit several claims for the same point with conflicting values (root mass density, root torsional stiffness, root axial stiffness, tip mass density), which looks like curve points and axis ticks being sampled indiscriminately. Neither set captures the mass center, neutral center or pitch axis chordwise curves of Figure 2-11, and the correct geometric/shear center values are absent from both. All plotted values are read visually from the figure and are approximate to about ±0.1 of each axis division.

baseline-first.note: Both sets contain the same 12 claims in substance: the second-order response, ωφn and ζφ formulas, the negative damping from the generator-torque controller, the negative ∂P/∂θ in Region 3, the PI gain expressions, and the design targets ωφn = 0.6 rad/s and ζφ = 0.6 to 0.7. The only difference is wording of the blade-pitch sensitivity claim (Set A gives 'aerodynamic property' as the value with the dependencies as conditions; Set B folds the dependencies into the value), and both are faithful to the page. Both sets also repeat the 0.6 rad/s and 0.6–0.7 targets under two entity names each, so both carry the same duplication issue.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets state the design targets twice (once as 'blade-pitch controller' and once as 'rotor-speed error response' targets) — the same fact under two names. Neither set captures the roles of the derivative/proportional/integral terms (effective inertia, damping, restoring) or the requirement that the proportional term compensate the generator-torque negative damping, which are notable facts on the page.

variant-first.note: The two sets are identical except for the framing of the ∂P/∂θ dependence claim: Set A states the dependence as the value, while Set B calls it an aerodynamic property and moves the dependence into conditions. Both capture the same facts from the same quote, so neither is more faithful overall. Both also repeat the ωφn = 0.6 rad/s and ζφ = 0.6–0.7 targets twice (once bound to the blade-pitch controller, once to the rotor-speed error response) and both omit the qualitative roles of the derivative, proportional and integral terms and the need to compensate the generator-torque negative damping.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets duplicate the Ref. [10] design targets (0.6 rad/s and 0.6–0.7) under two entity names; these should be merged. Both miss the page's statements that the derivative term increases effective drivetrain inertia, the proportional term adds damping, the integral term adds restoring, and that the negative damping from the generator-torque controller must be compensated by the proportional term. The text layer is heavily garbled around Eqs. (7-11)–(7-15), but the rendered equations in the image are legible and match the extracted formulas.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts (grade level 0'-0", finished floor 2'-9 1/2", section scales 3/8"=1'-0", revision table, lot number) and both repeat the grade-level, finished-floor and C1-scale facts several times. Set A adds an unsupported condition 'Reference datum' to a Grade Level claim, whereas Set B's section-scoped Grade Level conditions are supported because the GRADE LEVEL 0'-0" labels appear in both the West and East module sections. Set B's only extra flaw is one more duplicate Grade Level claim, so it is marginally cleaner on correctness.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets state Grade Level elevation three to four times and Finished Floor elevation / height-about-grade several times under slightly different entity/attribute spellings ('Grade Level' vs 'GRADE LEVEL', 'elevation' vs 'height above grade level'); these are the same two facts and should be deduplicated. Set A's 'conditions: Reference datum' is not text on the page. Nothing important on the sheet (e.g. sheet number A-301, sheet title BUILDING SECTIONS) appears to be missed by both beyond administrative data.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts (finished floor and grade level elevations, section scales, revision history), but A binds the grade-level elevations to the two sections where the markers actually appear (C1 West Module, A1 East Module) and adds the East Module scale claim. B instead attaches a single Grade Level claim to a "Reference datum" condition that the page never states, and omits the per-section grade-level readings. Both sets repeat the same elevations and scales several times under slightly different names.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets state Grade Level 0'-0" three times and Finished Floor 2'-9 1/2" twice with varying unit labels (ft-in / feet-inches / none), and Section C1 scale three times (as Section C1, SECTION - WEST MODULE, and a 'ratio' variant) — the same facts under two or three names. The elevation markers appear in both the C1 and A1 section views, so per-section binding (as in A) is the faithful reading. Revision-table and title-block entries are administrative and were treated as neutral.

baseline-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims, including the segment dimensions and the 5'-2 1/2" and 8'-0" dimensions, but they differ in a few claims. Set A states the deck module scale twice (duplicate) and gives the scaffold footing only a weak 'presence | installed' claim, while Set B correctly extracts its type as ADJUSTABLE and keeps the needed 'relative to Grade Level' condition on the First Floor 2'-4" elevation. Set B's only real blemishes are a stray space in the scale value and a truncated quote for the scaffold footing claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets bind the 1'-4 3/4" / 1'-4" / 1'-3 1/4" segment dimensions to 'RAILING ATTACHMENT', but on the page these segments belong to the 4'-0" dimension string of the A1 TYP. DECK MODULE plan; the shared 'deck connection | spacing | 1'-4 3/4" ... center to center' claim is likewise unsupported as stated. The 'scaffold footing | connection | frame' claim in both sets is vague about what connection is meant.

variant-first.note: A preserves two facts B loses or degrades: the scaffold footing's ADJUSTABLE type (B turns it into a trivial 'presence: installed' claim) and the condition that the FIRST FLR 2'-4" elevation is relative to GRADE LEVEL 0". B also states the TYP. DECK MODULE scale twice under two attribute names (drawing scale / scale), a clear duplicate. Both sets share the same misbindings — the 1'-4 3/4" / 1'-4" / 1'-3 1/4" chain and the 8'-0" dimension belong to the TYP. DECK MODULE detail (A1), not to RAILING ATTACHMENT or a 'deck connection spacing' — plus the same trivial self-referential component/presence claims and vague 'deck connection' entities. A's only extra defect is the truncated quote 'BLE SCAFFOLD FOOTING'.
variant-first.remarks: Shared misbindings: the dimension chain 4'-0" = 1'-4 3/4" + 1'-4" + 1'-3 1/4" and the vertical 8'-0" are drawn in detail A1 TYP. DECK MODULE, yet both sets bind them to RAILING ATTACHMENT (C1) or to a vague 'deck connection'; the invented 'center to center' condition on 1'-4 3/4" is not stated anywhere. Both sets also miss the 3/8" x 4" HEX THROUGH BOLT called out in A1 and the overall 4'-0" deck module width. Quotes such as 'RAILING POST BRACKET' and 'SCAFFOLD FOOTING' do not support the 'connection | frame' claims in either set (the connection is only inferable from the drawing), and 'CLEARVUE CABLE RAILING | component | CLEARVUE CABLE RAILING' / 'RAILING POST BRACKET | component | ...' are tautological. A's quote 'BLE SCAFFOLD FOOTING' is a mid-word fragment of 'ADJUSTABLE SCAFFOLD FOOTING', suggesting a text-layer/extraction clipping issue.

baseline-first.note: Both sets repeat the same facts many times (pipe diameter, bolt diameter, angle size, and plate thicknesses appear 2–4 times each) and both use the vague entity "structural element" for the 1'-8" and 1'-4 1/4" dimensions. Set A reads the values cleanly (3" pipe, 3/4" bolts, 1"/1/2"/3/8" plates, L3x3x1/4 angle, 4 X 3/8" cap plate), with only one unsupported claim (the bare 1/4" bound as "Crane Attachment Detail thickness/gap") and it omits the PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 plate. Set B does capture that plate, but six of its claims stuff label text into the value field ("3 DIA STD. PIPE", "3 DIA", "1/2 PL TYP", "3/8 PL TYP", "1 PL TYP", "3/4 DIA"), and one quote ("1\" PL") is truncated so it no longer supports the "typical" condition. On balance A is the more faithful set despite its one misbinding and its missing plate claim.
baseline-first.remarks: Both extractions are heavily duplicated: the same callout is re-emitted under several entity spellings (pipe/bolts/plate/angle), so 18-25 'claims' cover roughly 8 distinct facts. Both sets also miss the T.O. STEEL 11'-4" elevation and the small 3/8" dimension shown in the detail. Set B's recurring failure mode is copying the whole callout string (e.g. '3/8" PL TYP') into the value field instead of parsing the numeric value and unit; Set A's is binding bare dimension fragments (1/4") to the detail as a whole.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core crane-attachment facts (3" std pipe, (2) 3/4" bolts, L3x3x1/4 angle, 1"/1/2"/3/8" plates, 4 X 3/8" cap plate, and the 1'-8" and 1'-4 1/4" heights) and both repeat those facts heavily. Set A additionally captures the PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2 plate that B omits, but it pads its sample with label-contaminated values ('3/8 PL TYP', '1 PL TYP', '1/2 PL TYP', '3 DIA STD. PIPE', '3 DIA', '3/4 DIA') and states each fact up to four times. Set B is cleaner and more compact, though it invents a 'thickness/gap' attribute for the unlabeled 1/4" dimension. On balance B carries fewer wrong claims despite missing one real plate size.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets miss the 11'-4" T.O. STEEL elevation shown in the detail, and neither binds the standalone 3/8" and 1/4" dimension callouts on the left to a specific feature. Set A's misreads are mostly label-in-value formatting ('3/8 PL TYP' as a thickness), i.e. low-severity but counted per the misread category; its worst structural problem is duplication (plate 3/8" x4, pipe 3" x4, angle L3x3x1/4 x4, bolts 3/4" x4). Set B's 1/4" claim is unsupported as stated: the page shows 1/4" only as an unlabeled dimension, with no 'thickness/gap' attribute. Both use the vague entity 'structural element' for the two vertical dimensions, which are really heights/elevations of the attachment assembly.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical: 24 of the 25 shown claims match exactly, including the same series-connection conditions, the #10G bonding jumper gauge, and the same duplicated model/design facts. The only difference is the frameless-glass design claim: Set A gives the value 'FRAMLESS GLASS' (a clean reading of 'FRAMLESS GLASS DESIGN' under attribute 'design'), while Set B gives the garbled fragment 'FRAMLESS GLASS DESIG'. Both sets also share the same defects — the truncated model 'SUNPREME GX290 SOLA', the legend key '3' treated as an internal value/quantity, and the same facts stated twice under 'solar module' and 'PV Module'.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets read the hexagon '3' inside each module symbol as an 'internal value', 'value' or 'quantity'; per the LEGEND that '3' is the symbol key for the SUNPREME GX290 solar module, so those claims are misbound/trivial in both sets. Both also truncate the model name to 'SUNPREME GX290 SOLA' and state the model and frameless-glass design twice (once as 'solar module', once as 'PV Module'). The 'SOLAR ARRAY MOUNTING RAILS' leader points to the rail line generally, not specifically to SA3-1/SA3-2, so those two connection claims are weakly bound in both sets. The whole comparison turns on one truncated value, so the ranking is fragile.

variant-first.note: The two samples are identical except for one duplicated, low-value claim: A renders the frameless-glass design value as the mid-word truncation 'FRAMLESS GLASS DESIG' while B renders it 'FRAMLESS GLASS'. Both sets make the same misbindings (the 'SOLAR ARRAY MOUNTING RAILS' leader treated as a connection of SA3-1 and SA3-2), the same truncated model value ('SUNPREME GX290 SOLA'), and the same duplicates (model and design each stated under both 'PV Module' and 'solar module'; bare 'value | 3' claims repeating 'internal value | 3'). Neither omits an engineering fact the other captures, so the sets are effectively equivalent in correctness.
variant-first.remarks: Both extractions treat the '3' inside each hexagon inconsistently — as 'internal value', bare 'value', and 'quantity' — while the legend shows the hexagon-with-3 is the SUNPREME GX290 solar module symbol, i.e. a per-string module count; a single consistent attribute would be better. The 'SOLAR ARRAY MOUNTING RAILS' text is a general leader note about the array, not a connection of SA3-1/SA3-2. The text layer is heavily fragmented (polarity marks and labels separated from their symbols), so terminal/connection claims could not be fully verified from text alone and were judged mainly on plausibility against the image.

baseline-first.note: B is the cleaner set: it avoids A's five invented "location = wall" attributions for the tags EX, CT, GT, WO and RF, A's misreading of the graphic scale bar (0 1' 2' 4') as "scale = 4 ft", and A's duplicated claims (robe hook height stated twice, 10' - 3 15/16" stated as both "total width" and "dimension", MWK03 stated as both component label and panel identifier). Both sets, however, make the same serious misbinding: 8' - 9 7/16" is the overall height of the D5 North Kitchen Elevation, not the H1 robe hook mounting height, which the bathroom elevation gives as 4' - 0"; both also hang 8' - 6 13/16" and 7' - 6" on finish code P3 and put 2' - 8 9/16" (a top dimension of the A6 West Bathroom Elevation) under North Kitchen Elevation. B adds one claim of its own that is wrong (MWK03 called a wall/surface material/finish), but overall it loses fewer claims to misbinding and invention.
baseline-first.remarks: Both shown sets fabricate the quote 'H1 ROBE HOOK MOUNTING HEIGHT 8' - 9 7/16"' by joining a label in the bathroom elevation to a dimension from the D5 kitchen elevation; the sheet's actual H1 mounting height is 4' - 0". Both also miss other visible facts (BULKHEAD FIN. W/ P3, DIRTT BREATHE LIVING WALL 4'-0" W x 5'-6", SEE ARTWORK PKG FOR SIZE & MOUNT LOCATIONS, 17' - 3 1/8" West Kitchen total width), though some may sit in the unshown shared claims. The bathroom elevation at top left is cut off in the text layer ('ATHROOM ELEVATION'), so its detail number could not be read. Repeated values (2' - 6 3/8" x3-4, 10' - 3 15/16" x2) are handled inconsistently: A splits them into 'first/second instance' and duplicates, B into 'segment width 1/2/3'; neither ties them to a named elevation or segment.

baseline-first.note: Set B reads the plotted marker positions more faithfully, giving distinct x2 coordinates (NA 0.0, SC 0.1, GC -0.1, CG -0.2 m) and the elevated x3 of GC (0.05 m) that the figure shows, while Set A flattens every x3 to 0.0 m and omits all x2 coordinates, losing most of the figure's engineering content. Set B's only clear slip is SC x3 = 0.05 m, since the shear-center marker sits at about the same height as NA (≈0.0 m), below the CG/GC markers. Both sets capture the five visible layup materials and the 70% span section, but both drop Carbon UD from the legend and support numeric coordinates only with legend labels.
baseline-first.remarks: All coordinate values must be read off a small scatter plot with no tabulated numbers, so 0.0 vs 0.05 m distinctions are near the resolution limit; SC x3 in B and the CG/GC x3 = 0.0 in A are judged from marker heights relative to the x3 = 0 tick. Both sets omit the Carbon UD material shown in the legend, and B omits CG x3 while A omits every x2 coordinate. Quotes for the coordinate claims are legend labels (e.g. 'NA: Neutral Axes') and support the entity/attribute but not the numeric values, in both sets.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts and share the same errors: the 1/4" adjacent to the support plates is bound as plate thickness even though the plates are called out 11"X3/8" (3/8" thick), and the section label B-L1a-GF is recycled as a member label, detail label and connection identifier. Set B is modestly better because it preserves the Detail C1 condition on the L4X4X5/16 member, the 1/4" weld and the B-L1a-GF reference, and binds the (2) 3/4" bolts to the angle rather than a generic 'connection'. Set A instead adds a vague 'structural member | dimension | 1/4"' and a redundant second bolt-diameter claim, while B's extra claim (Detail C1 scale) is a harmless duplicate of a correct fact.
variant-first.remarks: Both sets read the '1/4"▽' markers as a slope and add invented 'top surface'/'bottom surface' conditions; the symbol is more likely a level/slope marker and the surface conditions are unsupported. The 1/4" next to '11"X3/8" CONT. SUPPORT PLATES' is a separate dimension (likely weld/gap), not plate thickness — both sets misbind it and then contradict themselves with the correct 3/8" thickness claim. Both sets omit the elevation callouts on the page (T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0") and the detail callouts 1 and 8 that scope the L3X3X1/4 connections.

baseline-first.note: The two sets are nearly identical in substance and share the same errors: both read the 1/4" slope symbols as a thickness (support plates, floor overhang) even though the plate is named 11"X3/8", and both treat the section-cut label B-L1a-GF as a detail reference and bind grid line "E" as a location. A is marginally more faithful in that it keeps the Detail C1 condition on the L4X4X5/16 and 1/4" claims and names the angle as the fastener owner, but it also repeats the C1 scale already stated under the West Roof Cantilever claim. B is slightly vaguer ("structural member | dimension | 1/4\"") and attaches the questionable condition "detail 8" (a detail callout bubble) to the L3X3X1/4 angle. Neither captures the T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4" or GRADE LEVEL 0" elevations shown on the page.
baseline-first.remarks: Both sets misread the two 1/4" slope (triangle) callouts in the A1 FLOOR OVERHANG DETAIL as thicknesses and as a slope of a generic "CANTILEVER DETAIL"; the correct reading is a 1/4" slope on the floor overhang, and the support plates are 11" wide x 3/8" thick per their own label. Both also duplicate the (2) 3/4" dia bolt fact under two names (angle connection / angle or connection fastener) and repeat the B-L1a-GF label as three separate trivial claims. Important facts both sets miss: T.O. STEEL elevation 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4", GRADE LEVEL 0". The 1/4" value near the L4X4X5/16/W8X10 junction is not identified on the page as a weld size, so the "weld size" claims in both sets are unsupported.

variant-first.note: Both sets share the same core claims and both fabricate the note-1 quote "1. ALL CU" to assert a copper material, when the page actually says current-carrying cable is USE-2, 10 GA. Set A adds two misbound claims treating the symbol number "3" as a connection target for SA1-6 and SA1-7, plus an SA1-10 terminal-polarity claim whose quote ("+") does not bind the polarity to that module. Set B formulates the 11-labels more accurately as interconnecting component values between the SA1-6/SA1-7 and SA2-19/SA2-20 pairs, and avoids A's extra misbindings. Both sets are otherwise near-identical, with the same duplicated "value 3 / component value 3" pairs and the same vague treatment of the in-symbol "3".
variant-first.remarks: Note 1 reads 'ALL CURRENT CARRYING CABLE IS USE-2, 10.G.A' but both sets quote it as '1. ALL CU' and derive a copper-material claim — a shared fabrication/garble worth fixing in the extractor. The in-symbol '3' (circle inside every module) and the '11' callouts at the four inter-module junctions are ambiguous symbols (legend/detail references rather than engineering values), yet both sets emit many 'value 3' claims and treat 11 as a connection endpoint; these should be classified as symbol references, not values. Important page facts (SUNPREME GX290 module, frameless glass design per E-502, #10G bonding jumper, USE-2 10 GA cable) are absent from the shown samples, though they may sit in the shared unshown claims.
